import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 770

*References:*
 - [erdosproblems.com/770](https://www.erdosproblems.com/770)
 - [Er49d] Erdös, P. "On the strong law of large numbers." Transactions of the American Mathematical
    Society 67.1 (1949): 51-56.
 - [Ma66] Matsuyama, Noboru. "On the strong law of large numbers." Tohoku Mathematical Journal,
    Second Series 18.3 (1966): 259-269.
-/

open Set ENat Filter

namespace Erdos770


/-- Let $h n$ be the minimal number such that $2 ^ n - 1, \dots, h(n) ^ n - 1$
are collectively coprime. -/
noncomputable def h (n : ℕ) : ℕ∞ := sInf {m | 2 < m ∧
  ((Finset.Icc 2 m.toNat).image fun i => (i ^ n - 1)).gcd id = 1}

/-- `n + 1` is prime iff `h n = n + 1`. This is described as 'easy to see' in [Er74b]. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem Nat.Prime.h_eq_add_one {n : ℕ} (hn : 2 < n) : h n = n + 1 ↔ (n + 1).Prime := by
  sorry

/-- For odd `n`, the values of `h n` form an unbounded set.
This is described as 'easy to see' in [Er74b]. -/
@[category textbook, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_770.variants.odd_h_unbounded : Unbounded (· ≤ ·) (ENat.toNat '' (h '' Odd)):= by
  sorry


/-- For every prime `p`, does the density of integers with `h n = p` exist? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_770.parts.i : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ p : ℕ, p.Prime → ∃ a, HasDensity {n | h n = p} a := by
  sorry

/-- Does `liminf h n = ∞`? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_770.parts.ii : answer(sorry) ↔ liminf h atTop = ⊤ := by
  sorry

/-- Is it true that if `p` is the greatest prime such that `p - 1 ∣ n` and `p > n ^ ε`, then
`h n = p`? -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_770.parts.iii : answer(sorry) ↔ ∀ ε > 0, ∀ᶠ n in atTop,
    let p := sSup {m : ℕ | m.Prime ∧ m - 1 ∣ n}
    p > (n : ℝ) ^ (ε : ℝ) → h n = p := by
  sorry

/-- It is probably true that `h n = 3` for infinitely many `n`. -/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem erdos_770.variants.three : {n | h n = 3}.Infinite := by
  sorry

end Erdos770

findings.description: The extra condition `2 < m` changes the minimum at `n = 1`. The singleton `{2^1 - 1} = {1}` already has gcd 1, so the source's least endpoint is 2. The Lean definition instead forces `h n ≥ 3` and gives `h 1 = 3`. I proved both `Erdos770.h 1 = 3` and that replacing `<` with `≤` gives value 2. The definitions agree for every `n ≥ 2`, so this is a boundary defect in the definition, not a defect in the asymptotic research questions.
findings.source_evidence: https://www.erdosproblems.com/latex/770 defines h(n) as minimal such that 2^n−1,3^n−1,…,h(n)^n−1 are mutually coprime, without imposing h(n)>2. Erdős, [Er74b], §II, p.199 (https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1974-27.pdf), likewise defines the smallest such integer and states that h(n)=n+1 whenever n+1 is prime.
findings.suggested_fix: Change `sInf {m | 2 < m ∧ ...}` to `sInf {m | 2 ≤ m ∧ ...}`. This restores the source's minimum at n=1 while leaving all values for n≥2 unchanged.

findings.description: The module bibliography lists [Er49d] and [Ma66], two papers about the strong law of large numbers, rather than the paper containing these number-theoretic questions. The relevant [Er74b], cited in the theorem docstrings, is missing from the bibliography.
findings.source_evidence: The problem page https://www.erdosproblems.com/770 cites [Er74b]. Erdős's 'Remarks on some problems in number theory', §II, pp.199–200, contains the definition of h, both elementary observations, and the research questions. The listed 1949 and 1966 papers instead discuss Fourier series and almost-everywhere convergence of averages of periodic functions.
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the two unrelated references with [Er74b]: Erdős, P., 'Remarks on some problems in number theory', Math. Balkanica 4 (1974), 197–202, especially §II, pp.199–200; https://users.renyi.hu/~p_erdos/1974-27.pdf.

reformulations.difference: The theorem restricts the source's elementary equivalence to `2 < n`.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Let h₀ denote the source's minimum, formalized with `2 ≤ m`. I proved h₀(n)=h(n) for n≥2, h₀(1)=2, and h(2)=3. Thus the source's positive-index equivalence has two elementary true boundary cases, n=1 and n=2, and its remaining cases are precisely the restricted Lean statement. The restriction is not a separate statement defect, despite the boundary error in h itself.

reformulations.difference: Unboundedness is expressed using the image under `ENat.toNat`, which maps infinity to zero.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: I proved h(n)<⊤ for every positive n. For n≥2, set m=2^n−1≥3; the prefix includes m and m^n−1, which are coprime, giving a finite eligible endpoint. The case n=1 has h(1)=3. Consequently toNat preserves every value occurring at an odd index. Unfolding the images and Unbounded gives exactly `∀ M : ℕ, ∃ n : ℕ, Odd n ∧ (M : ℕ∞) < h n`; this equivalence was proved in Lean.

reformulations.difference: The greatest prime is represented by a natural-number `sSup`, and the informal condition is explicitly quantified for each fixed positive ε and all sufficiently large n.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: For n>0 the prime set contains 2, and every member m satisfies m−1≤n, hence m≤n+1. It is therefore nonempty and bounded, and its natural supremum is its greatest member. The exceptional unbounded set at n=0 is irrelevant under `∀ᶠ n in atTop`. I proved an iff replacing the let-bound supremum with universal quantification over a prime satisfying IsGreatest. The source discussion on 21 September 2025 explicitly confirms the sufficiently-large-n interpretation for each ε and gives n=4044 as a small-value obstruction to an all-n reading.

sources_consulted: Ailon and Rudnick, 'Torsion points on curves and common divisors of a^k−1 and b^k−1', Conjecture A; LaTeX source at https://arxiv.org/e-print/math/0202102
review.notes: Checked every declaration and the repository checklist. The research questions are unchanged by the one-point discrepancy in h: natural densities, liminf, eventual assertions, and infinitude ignore finitely many initial indices. The source still records the questions as open; its listed proof claim is explicitly partial. The files /workspace/review/boundary.lean and computations.lean compile successfully. Boundary and equivalence proofs were checked to have no sorryAx dependency, including h(0)=⊤, finiteness for positive inputs, and the equivalence of ENat liminf=⊤ with convergence to infinity. Website pages were read through Jina's renderer after direct Cloudflare failures, preserving mathematics through the LaTeX page or HTML math attributes. The reviewed file remains identical to the committed version.

submission.summary: Changed the endpoint condition from `2 < m` to `2 ≤ m`, restoring `h 1 = 2`. Also replaced the unrelated bibliography entries with the verified [Er74b] reference. The requested compile succeeds with only existing `sorry` warnings; separate scratch proofs confirm `h 1 = 2` and `h 0 = ⊤`.
